### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, touching **60** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-messaging/src/fan-out-system-context.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**71** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ca09de55d106b6ddd18c0e704ce40c96b26bccc`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-messaging/src/fan-out-system-context.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 51 pages)`, `organization_id (literal, 40 pages)`
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **8** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ca09de55d106b6ddd18c0e704ce40c96b26bccc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7c65129f98f03d8bf8fdd0e9d83633159da22dc5` — the merge of head `199aa958dfea4d3fab7368022495901a76e8fc96` into base `2ca09de55d106b6ddd18c0e704ce40c96b26bccc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7c65129f98f03d8bf8fdd0e9d83633159da22dc5 && git checkout 7c65129f98f03d8bf8fdd0e9d83633159da22dc5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2ca09de55d106b6ddd18c0e704ce40c96b26bccc 199aa958dfea4d3fab7368022495901a76e8fc96 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2ca09de55d106b6ddd18c0e704ce40c96b26bccc && git merge --no-ff 199aa958dfea4d3fab7368022495901a76e8fc96

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ca09de55d106b6ddd18c0e704ce40c96b26bccc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2ca09de55d106b6ddd18c0e704ce40c96b26bccc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `b4d4802884420759c3cf164217ffdea1e1a9a43e`
Local-runs: probe — the brief asked for the new tests to be run. On a scratch worktree at this head (JS-only build of the dependency closure), in `@objectstack/service-messaging`: `in-app-message-routes.integration.test.ts`, `in-app-message-action.test.ts` and `preference-options-routes.integration.test.ts`, 3 files, 46/46 passed. In `@objectstack/core` (`--project repo`): `credential-use-client-doors.pin.test.ts`, 4/4 passed. On the previous head `3bae7b7a` the census failed 2 of 4, the same as that head's red `Test Core (6/8)`.
Scope: the `Clause-②: yes` declaration (PR body and `.changeset/32445-in-app-message-action.md`), read across the diff that implements it: `packages/services/service-messaging/src/{in-app-message-routes,messaging-request-caller,messaging-service-plugin,preference-options-routes,messaging-route-ledger,fan-out-system-context}.ts`, the two new test files and the ledger conformance test, `packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-notification.object.ts`, `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`, `packages/core/src/security/credential-use-client-doors.pin.test.ts` (the delta from `3bae7b7a`). Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `resolveRequestExecutionContext` / `resolveAuthzContext` (core), `actionPermissionError` and the `type: 'api'` forward (runtime), the `org:members` resolver and the preference filter (service-messaging on main), `ActionAiSchema` (spec). Not reviewed: translations and `content/docs/**` (prose face, the seat's ACCEPT).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Card premises checked.** Ruling 6810324463 letter A asks for a Setup action "Send in-app message" with a multi-user picker or an everyone switch, title, body, severity and link, for organization administrators only, calling `emit()`. The diff delivers each part. Ruling 6670707546 item B exists and recommends `setup.write` in the caller's current organization as the gate for an organization-scoped admin door. Two shipped doors use that same capability: `RECORD_CURRENCY_BACKFILL_CAPABILITY` and `ORGANIZATION_CLIENT_ADDRESS_CAPABILITY`. Claim amendment 6833542858 says to return `needs_decision` only if the door needs a gate shape the platform does not already declare. `setup.write` is already declared, so that condition is not met. The PR body says plainly that a custom set granting `setup.write` is admitted too. Accepted.
- **Route shape.** `POST /api/v1/messaging/in-app-messages` is mounted once, by `MessagingServicePlugin` at `kernel:ready`. No other package serves that path (route rule 1). When no HTTP server is registered, the plugin logs that the door is absent (rule 3). The closed query set is empty and any parameter is refused with `400`; this matches the precedent preference-options door (rule 5). The ledger row is `server-only`, and the conformance test enumerates the new registrar.
- **Envelope, codes and statuses.** Every answer goes through `sendOk` / `sendError` / `sendServerFault`, so the route-envelope declaration `{0,0,0}` is correct. The codes and statuses are: `UNAUTHENTICATED`/401; the held-sign-in code/403; `PERMISSION_DENIED`/403 for the missing capability and for no current organization; `VALIDATION_ERROR`/400 for the query, the body and non-members; `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`/503; `INTERNAL_ERROR`/500. The relayed store and API-key lifecycle refusals keep their own status and code. Success is `{ notificationId, recipients, delivered, enqueued, failed }`. The tests assert both `status` and `error.code` against `ApiErrorSchema` / `envelopeViolations`.
- **One fact for listing and admitting.** The action's `requiredPermissions: ['setup.write']` is checked against `ExecutionContext.systemPermissions`, both by the action doors (`actionPermissionError`) and by the console's client-side gate. The door reads the same list on the same context, after the platform's one composition. `in-app-message-action.test.ts` pins the action and the door together (target, capability, params equal to the body keys, severity options), and ablation 6 in the PR body shows the pin turning red. Members do not see the action, and the door refuses them `403` before any read. A real-composition test covers this.
- **The organization never comes from the caller's input.** The organization is `ExecutionContext.tenantId`, and only the session's active organization or the API key's organization sets it. Both are checked against the caller's current memberships, and capabilities are resolved for that organization only. The body cannot name an organization: `organizationId` and `organization_id` are refused by name, and so is every other key outside the set. No header is read for the organization. "Everyone" emits `org:members` with `organizationId` set to the caller's organization, and the resolver filters on that id alone. The tests check this boundary in both directions on a real `ObjectQL`/`SqlDriver`, ablations 1 and 2 confirm it, and my local run passed. A picked id is checked against `sys_member` of that organization (chunks of 100, filtered on `organization_id`, projected to `user_id`) and then sent as `user:ID`, so it cannot be read as a selector or an address. A caller with `setup.write` in org A cannot reach org B.
- **The body is a closed key set.** It accepts exactly `{ everyone, recipients, title, body, severity, link }`. An unknown key is refused by name, never dropped. Exactly one of `everyone` and `recipients` is required. All 17 refusal cases send nothing, and the tests assert no `emit()`, no membership read and no inbox row.
- **Delta from `3bae7b7a` (reviewed in full; `git diff 3bae7b7a b4d48028`).** One commit changes one file, `credential-use-client-doors.pin.test.ts`, +6/−2. The census entry for `preference-options-routes.ts` moves to `messaging-request-caller.ts`, the module the `resolveRequestExecutionContext` call was moved into. Its `calls` count stays `{ resolveRequestExecutionContext: 1 }`, and the door text names both messaging doors. The pin is still `preference-options-routes.integration.test.ts`. That test asserts the `transport.remoteAddress` hand-off through the shared function, and the in-app door calls the same function. The previous head's must-fix (that census red on `Test Core (6/8)`) is resolved: the census passes locally. The check-runs for this head were still in progress when this was written, so landing still needs them all green.
- nit N4 — the census pin reaches the shared module only through the preference-options door. No test drives the in-app door through `resolveMessagingCaller` with an API key and asserts `transport.remoteAddress`. The plugin wiring is one line, so this is optional.

### ② Semver level

- Both declaration lines appear at line start in both carriers: `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, in the PR body and the changeset body. `Clause-②: yes` is correct: a new public REST route with its own body set, refusals and answer is new contract surface. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct: `send_in_app_message` is a platform object's declaration made only of existing action keys (`type: 'api'`, `target`, `requiredPermissions`, `params`, `ai`). It adds no key, accepted value or metadata type that an author could write. Under AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, the kind `none` takes `patch`, so `'@objectstack/service-messaging': patch` and `'@objectstack/platform-objects': patch` are the correct levels, and both are published packages the diff moves. Nothing is narrowed or removed, so no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 marker is owed. The deviation (one `MODULES` row in `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`) is the gate's own requirement for a new route module, and it ships nothing.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **should-fix S1 — an agent can trigger the broadcast with no confirmation step.** The action sets `ai.exposed: true` but not `ai.requiresConfirmation`. By `ActionAiSchema`'s default, an AI call is gated only when the action looks destructive (`mode: 'delete'` or `variant: 'danger'`), and this action is `variant: 'primary'`. So an agent acting for an administrator can send to every member of the organization, which cannot be undone, with no human step. Fix: `ai: { exposed: true, requiresConfirmation: true, … }`, and add an assertion to `in-app-message-action.test.ts`. An API key is admitted with its owner's grants in the key's own organization, the same as the precedent doors. Nothing more is owed there.
- nit N1 — the count can read as success when nothing went out. `recipients` counts distinct recipients across all `deliveries`, including failed enqueues (the answer also carries `failed`). An `org:members` resolution that fails inside the resolver, or an organization with no inbox channel available, answers `200` with `recipients: 0`, and the console confirms "Message sent. Recipients: 0". Worth a sentence in the docs, or a follow-up item on the dialog card #32796.
- nit N2 — the limits on title (255), body (10,000), link (255) and recipient count (1,000) are bounded and tested. A single recipient id has no length bound of its own and is echoed in the non-member refusal. The request-body size limit still caps it. Optional per-id cap.
- nit N3 — there is no limit on how often a sender can send. The ruling did not ask for one, and the PR body says so. Recorded as an accepted deviation.
- Default Organization and inactive organization: nothing is owed. `org:members` reads the `sys_member` rows of the caller's current organization, and no current organization is refused before any read. The authz resolution has no "inactive organization" state that this door could cross. Preference opt-outs: the topic `org.announcement` goes through the preference filter like any other topic. `critical` skips quiet hours and digests but not a mute, so the changeset's "turned off ⇒ not sent, not counted" is true.
- Author: the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author note is owed.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-a3rtmw`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgWRcTEB3toGxnWvuvX`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `199aa958dfea4d3fab7368022495901a76e8fc96`
Local-runs: probe — the brief asked for the new tests to be run at the head. On a scratch worktree at `199aa958` (`@objectstack/platform-objects` rebuilt JS-only), in `@objectstack/service-messaging`: `vitest run src/in-app-message-routes.integration.test.ts src/in-app-message-action.test.ts`, 2 files, 38/38 passed (the 37 earlier tests plus the new confirmation pin).
Scope: delta review, `git diff b4d48028 199aa958`: one commit, two files, `packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-notification.object.ts` (+6/−1) and `packages/services/service-messaging/src/in-app-message-action.test.ts` (+10/−2). This delta review completes this seat's full review of the declaration face. The full review was at `3bae7b7a` (FAIL: must-fix M1 and should-fix S1). The delta review at `b4d48028` closed M1 and left S1 open. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `ActionAiSchema.requiresConfirmation` (spec). The translation bundles were checked: none of them carries the action's `ai.description`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **S1 is resolved.** `send_in_app_message` now declares `ai: { exposed: true, requiresConfirmation: true, description }`. `ActionAiSchema` documents `requiresConfirmation: true` as the explicit override that gates an action that would otherwise run without confirmation. An agent's call to this action therefore waits for a person to confirm it. The `ai.description` ends with "Ask the human to confirm before calling." A comment above `ai` says why the default would not ask.
- **The pin.** `in-app-message-action.test.ts` adds `expect(action!.ai).toMatchObject({ exposed: true, requiresConfirmation: true })`, and the dev reports the ablation red and then restored. It passed in my local run.
- **Nothing else moved.** The delta has no change to the door, its route, the body set, the gate, the organization rule, the envelope, the ledger or the changeset. Every judgment in the earlier records stands: the gate reads the same fact for listing and admitting; the organization is only the caller's verified current one; the body is a closed key set; the codes and statuses are as declared. The census move from `b4d48028` is unchanged.
- **Check-runs at this head.** When this was written: 9 success, 9 skipped, 19 in progress, none failed. That includes Lint & Repo Gates, Type Check · workspace and the Test Core shard plan. Landing still needs all of them to finish green. The 2 failures on the earlier head `b4d48028` (`TypeScript Type Check`, `Test UI`) were recorded beside 29 runs cancelled by the new push. They are not on the current head, so no action is owed for them.

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged. `requiresConfirmation` is an existing key on a platform object's own declaration, so it is not new authorable surface. `Metadata-protocol: none` ⇒ `patch` on both packages stays correct. `Clause-②: yes` is correct and stays in both carriers. This delta owes no new changeset sentence. The changeset does not mention agent confirmation; it could, but that is prose.

### ③ Boundary flags

- An agent as the actor: closed by S1's fix, above.
- The nits stay nits and go to a follow-up card:
  - N1: the `recipients` count includes failed enqueues, and the door answers `200` with 0 when the member lookup fails or no inbox channel is available.
  - N2: a single recipient id has no length limit and is echoed back in the refusal.
  - N3: there is no send-rate limit (not asked for by the ruling).
  - N4: no API-key test drives the in-app door through the shared caller resolution.
- The PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author note is owed.

> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；

> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
